Tree‑Ising: How Bit‑Level Ising Edits Are Turning Model Repair into a One‑Click Operation
Lead
Fixing a seven‑billion‑parameter model’s hallucination loop took just fifty forward passes. A senior engineer at OpenAI revealed this breakthrough in a Slack thread on 12 Nov 2026. The method—Tree‑Ising—flips bits in a model’s BF16 weight tensors the way a physicist flips spins in an Ising lattice. entry.title: Make your website readable by AI search: robots.txt, llms.txt and schema
entry.summary: More people now ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity instead of typing into Google. If your site blocks those crawlers or explains itself badly, you will not be mentioned. At DiziGoo, a digital marketing and software company in Bareilly, India, we made our own site AI-friendly and these are the steps that mattered. Check your robots.txt. If you want to be cited in AI answers, allow the bots that fetch pages for answers, such as GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot and Google-Extended. Also check your CDN: some platforms add their own managed robots.txt that can override yours, so open /robots.txt in a browser after every change. llms.txt is a plain text file at the root of your site that summarises who you are, what you offer and your best pages, written for machines. Keep it factual: business name, location, services, links to guides, contact details. Use schema.org JSON-LD for Organization, LocalBusiness, Service, FAQPage and BreadcrumbList. Keep the name, address and phone identical to your Google Business Profile. Machines trust data that matches everywhere. AI answers quote pages that answer one question clearly. Use short headings that are real questions, answer in the first two sentences, and keep facts like services, locations and timelines in text, not only in images. Claim your Google Business Profile, Bing Places and company directories, and publish helpful articles. OpenAI has also started Businesses in ChatGPT, where a company can claim a verified profile. We have started that process too. Search your brand and your service plus your city in an AI assistant once a week, and note whether you are mentioned. Fix the page that should have answered. None of this needs a big budget, only consistency. More on how we approach AI search and SEO: https://dizigoo.com/services/seo/ By Akash Gupta, founder of DiziGoo (digital marketing, websites, software and AI automation), Bareilly and Pilibhit, India.

entry.title: The project stops at 80% the moment you stop doubting you can finish it
entry.summary: @csm18 answered the question at the end of my last post with something I have not seen written down before. He starts a new project because the idea is big and he has never built anything like it. Maybe he will not be able to. That uncertainty is the fire. It gets him to start without asking whether the thing is practical. Then comes the point where he can see the progress is real. If he keeps going, it will be finished. And at exactly that point: once I know I can do it, I start to think if I can, then why should I worry about it. Whenever I want to I will, not now. The fire goes out. entry.title: Node.js Object PUT vs Multipart Upload — Pick Multipart for Large App Backups
entry.summary: Short answer: use multipart upload for large Node.js backup archives, and keep the upload ledger in your job database so a worker can resume, complete, or deliberately abort the transfer. The deciding constraint is throughput under interruption. A developer-tools platform may turn thousands of receipt images and records into one tar.gz, then retain that exact file for an audit. Holding the archive in memory or restarting one giant PUT after a broken connection makes the retry unit needlessly large. Multipart changes the retry unit from “the whole audit archive” to “one numbered part.” This is an operational choice, not a promise that multipart wins for every object. Small receipts can stay on a single PUT. Large backup bundles should not. Picture the original worker as a three-box diagram …

entry.title: SaaS Subscriber Delivery: Simple Queue Retries, Backoff, and DLQ Isolation
entry.summary: For an edtech shipment-update fan-out, use at-least-once delivery with idempotent subscriber sends, a small retry budget, exponential backoff with jitter, and a dead-letter queue (DLQ) for exhausted jobs. That is the least complex policy that keeps a temporary downstream failure from becoming either a lost notification or an infinite retry loop. The important choice is the unit of work. Create one immutable job per subscriber, not one job for the whole shipment audience. A worker can then acknowledge successful subscribers independently while delaying only the failed ones. The shipment event carries a stable ID; each child job adds the subscriber ID and channel.
